## 01. Impeccable — Design taste for AI coding agents

- **Category:** Design
- **Made by:** pbakaus
- **Source:** https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable
- **Page:** https://ai-resources.vercel.app/tools/impeccable.html
- **Install / run:** `npx impeccable install`

**Why use Impeccable?**
Every model ships the same website: cream hero, gradient text, three identical cards. Impeccable gives your agent an actual design education: one skill, 23 commands, and 60 deterministic detectors that catch AI anti-patterns the moment they're written.

**When should you use Impeccable?**
Any frontend work you do with an agent. Audit before shipping, run polish passes after building, and let its edit-hooks flag design lapses in real time while you work.

**How do you install and use Impeccable?**
1. Run the installer in your project — it detects Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and more.
2. Run /impeccable init once so it learns your product and users.
3. Build, then finish with /impeccable audit or /impeccable polish.

**Curator's note:** Its detector ran on every edit of this page.

---

## 02. Superpowers — Engineering discipline for Claude Code

- **Category:** Workflow
- **Made by:** obra
- **Source:** https://github.com/obra/superpowers
- **Page:** https://ai-resources.vercel.app/tools/superpowers.html
- **Install / run:** `claude plugin install superpowers@claude-plugins-official`

**Why use Superpowers?**
Raw agents jump straight to code and guess. Superpowers makes them work like senior engineers: brainstorm the design first, write the plan, test-drive the implementation, review before merging. The difference shows up in week-two maintainability.

**When should you use Superpowers?**
Any feature bigger than a one-liner. It earns its keep on greenfield builds and gnarly debugging, where process beats enthusiasm.

**How do you install and use Superpowers?**
1. Install the plugin from the official marketplace.
2. Start any task — it routes through brainstorming and planning skills automatically.
3. Follow the checkpoints; approve the design before code gets written.

**Curator's note:** This site went through its brainstorm → plan → build flow.

---

## 03. Spec-Kit — Spec-driven development, by GitHub

- **Category:** Workflow
- **Made by:** github
- **Source:** https://github.com/github/spec-kit
- **Page:** https://ai-resources.vercel.app/tools/spec-kit.html
- **Install / run:** `uvx --from git+https://github.com/github/spec-kit.git specify init`

**Why use Spec-Kit?**
Vibe-coding drifts: by feature three, the agent is guessing what you meant in feature one. Spec-Kit inverts the relationship: an executable spec becomes the source of truth and implementations are derived from it.

**When should you use Spec-Kit?**
Multi-session projects, team work, anything where “what we're building” has to outlive a single chat context.

**How do you install and use Spec-Kit?**
1. Install the specify CLI (needs uv).
2. Run specify init inside your project.
3. Drive with /speckit.specify → /speckit.plan → /speckit.implement in your agent.

**Curator's note:** The spec survives. Chat context doesn't.

---

## 04. Chrome DevTools MCP — Gives your coding agent eyes in the browser

- **Category:** Agents & MCP
- **Made by:** ChromeDevTools
- **Source:** https://github.com/ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp
- **Page:** https://ai-resources.vercel.app/tools/chrome-devtools-mcp.html
- **Install / run:** `claude mcp add chrome-devtools npx chrome-devtools-mcp@latest`

**Why use Chrome DevTools MCP?**
An agent that can't see the page is coding blind, claiming fixes it never verified. This official MCP server hands it real Chrome: console errors, network requests, performance traces, screenshots, live DOM.

**When should you use Chrome DevTools MCP?**
Debugging web apps, chasing Core Web Vitals, and every “make a change, prove it actually rendered” loop.

**How do you install and use Chrome DevTools MCP?**
1. Add the MCP server to your agent's config.
2. Ask the agent to open your page and read the console.
3. Let it trace, screenshot, and verify its own work before it reports done.

**Curator's note:** The single biggest upgrade to agent frontend work I know.

---

## 05. Context7 — Current library docs, injected at generation time

- **Category:** Agents & MCP
- **Made by:** upstash
- **Source:** https://github.com/upstash/context7
- **Page:** https://ai-resources.vercel.app/tools/context7.html
- **Install / run:** `claude mcp add context7 -- npx -y @upstash/context7-mcp`

**Why use Context7?**
Models memorize last year's APIs and hallucinate the diff. Context7 pulls version-specific, up-to-date documentation straight into the prompt, so generated code compiles against the library you actually installed.

**When should you use Context7?**
Coding against anything that moves fast: Next.js, Tailwind, LangChain, any SDK younger than the model's training cutoff.

**How do you install and use Context7?**
1. Add the MCP server to your agent.
2. Append “use context7” to a prompt, or let a rule auto-invoke it.
3. Get code written against live docs instead of training-data memories.

**Curator's note:** Killed my “that method was renamed months ago” class of bugs.

---

## 06. Repomix — Your whole repo, packed into one AI-readable file

- **Category:** Coding
- **Made by:** yamadashy
- **Source:** https://github.com/yamadashy/repomix
- **Page:** https://ai-resources.vercel.app/tools/repomix.html
- **Install / run:** `npx repomix@latest`

**Why use Repomix?**
Context is the bottleneck. Repomix flattens an entire codebase into one structured file (directory tree, token counts, .gitignore respected, secrets scanned out) sized for pasting into any model.

**When should you use Repomix?**
Second opinions from web chats, code review by a model with no repo access, onboarding an agent to unfamiliar code.

**How do you install and use Repomix?**
1. Run it at the repo root.
2. Grab repomix-output.xml.
3. Paste it into the model of your choice; add --compress for big repos.

**Curator's note:** My “let another model sanity-check this” button.

---

## 07. Agent-Reach — Your agent, unblocked on the real internet

- **Category:** Agents & MCP
- **Made by:** Panniantong
- **Source:** https://github.com/Panniantong/Agent-Reach
- **Page:** https://ai-resources.vercel.app/tools/agent-reach.html
- **Install / run:** `Install Agent Reach: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Panniantong/agent-reach/main/docs/install.md`

**Why use Agent-Reach?**
The useful internet is walled: X wants API fees, Reddit blocks server IPs, video sites geo-fence. Agent-Reach ships the most reliable access path for each platform — chosen, installed, and health-checked — behind one interface.

**When should you use Agent-Reach?**
Research agents that need to actually read tweets, Reddit threads, and YouTube transcripts, or sweep several platforms in one run.

**How do you install and use Agent-Reach?**
1. Paste the install prompt below into your agent — it self-installs.
2. It detects your environment and reports what's reachable.
3. Ask for content by URL or search; it picks the working path.

**Curator's note:** Turns “I can't access that site” into an answer.

---

## 08. LLM Wiki — A second brain your model maintains for you

- **Category:** Knowledge
- **Made by:** karpathy
- **Source:** https://gist.github.com/karpathy/442a6bf555914893e9891c11519de94f
- **Page:** https://ai-resources.vercel.app/tools/llm-wiki.html

**Why use LLM Wiki?**
RAG re-reads everything on every question and synthesizes nothing. Karpathy's pattern makes the LLM maintain a persistent markdown wiki over your sources: ingest, cross-link, flag contradictions. Knowledge compiles once and stays current.

**When should you use LLM Wiki?**
Building a durable personal knowledge base out of notes, papers, and bookmarks that should get better with every source you add.

**How do you install and use LLM Wiki?**
1. Read the gist — it's a pattern, not a package.
2. Write your schema doc: how pages, entities, and links should be structured.
3. Point your agent at new sources to ingest; query the wiki, lint it periodically.

**Curator's note:** The rare idea that improves the longer you run it.

---

## 09. Humanizer — Deletes the AI accent from your writing

- **Category:** Writing
- **Made by:** blader
- **Source:** https://github.com/blader/humanizer
- **Page:** https://ai-resources.vercel.app/tools/humanizer.html
- **Install / run:** `npx skills add blader/humanizer --global`

**Why use Humanizer?**
Em-dash chains, “it's not X, it's Y”, bold on everything: readers smell AI prose instantly. Humanizer strips 33 documented patterns of machine writing and can calibrate to your voice from samples of your own work.

**When should you use Humanizer?**
The last pass before anything goes public: posts, documentation, emails, portfolio copy.

**How do you install and use Humanizer?**
1. Install it as a skill or Claude Code plugin.
2. Run /humanizer on pasted text or point it at a file.
3. Feed it a few writing samples once, so rewrites keep your voice.

**Curator's note:** The final gate before anything ships with my name on it.

---

## 10. Figma MCP — Your design file, readable by your coding agent

- **Category:** Design
- **Made by:** Figma
- **Source:** https://developers.figma.com/docs/figma-mcp-server/
- **Page:** https://ai-resources.vercel.app/tools/figma-mcp.html
- **Install / run:** `claude mcp add --transport http figma https://mcp.figma.com/mcp`

**Why use Figma MCP?**
Screenshot handoff makes agents guess: they eyeball spacing, invent hex values, and rebuild components you already shipped. Figma's official MCP server hands the agent the real source instead — variables, components, layout data, and Code Connect mappings — and it writes back to canvas, so the loop runs both directions.

**When should you use Figma MCP?**
Any build that starts from a design file, and any time production drift needs pulling back to the system. Select a frame, point the agent at it, and review what it generates against the tokens rather than the picture.

**How do you install and use Figma MCP?**
1. Add the remote server to your agent (or install the Figma plugin, if your client offers one).
2. Open the Figma desktop or web file and select the frame you want built.
3. Ask your agent to implement the selection; it reads variables and components instead of pixels.

**Curator's note:** The handoff step I stopped doing by hand.
